Resolves #19246

`DockCrossWindowWitnessNL` names the error its harness's synthetic windows provoke: `workerErrors.expect(/Target worker 'cw-win-a' does not exist\./)`, with one comment line saying why. The harness registers `cw-win-a` / `cw-win-b` in one App Worker and drives the real `TabSortZone`, whose window-drag calls for `cw-win-a` reach a main thread that cannot route to a window that never existed. The engine is right to surface that (`worker.Base#isDeparture` settles only a window that was there and left). The spec was the one red left in #17844's "teardown into a departed window" class; the other five pass at dev since #19061 / #19073.

Evidence: L2 (the spec run headless at the head with the runtime root bound, plus a mutation arm) → L2 required (test-only; no runtime-verify ACs). No residuals.

Micro-review eligible: test-only — one scoped expectation and its comment line, no engine change.

## AC Evidence
| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | outside-CI (NL specs are deselected in CI): at the head, `NEO_AGENTOS_RUNTIME_ROOT=… npx playwright test -c test/playwright/playwright.config.e2e.mjs --workers=1 …/DockCrossWindowWitnessNL.spec.mjs` → 1 passed. The nine witness assertions are unchanged, and the two named `cw-win-a` errors still occur (the spec's own `BROWSER JS ERROR` lines). |
| AC-2 | outside-CI, mutation: the pattern changed to `cw-win-z` → 1 failed (the two `cw-win-a` errors are unexpected again); restored → green. The gate still fails any error the expectation does not name. |

## Deltas from ticket
None substantive.

## Test Evidence
- The class census at dev `a9abb6c1dc`: `SharedWorkerRemoteReplay`, `DockCrossWindowWitnessNL`, `WindowOps`, `WorkstationReclaimEmbodimentNL`, `WorkstationTopologyGroupsNL` (headless, `--workers=1`) gave 13 passed, 1 failed, the one this PR fixes.
- Why it was a page error: the harness runs dedicated workers, so the call reached main. Main's forward replied with the rejection, the rejection went unhandled in the App Worker, and Playwright reports a dedicated worker's uncaught error as `pageerror` carrying the cloned Error's main-thread stack (the trace shows two `pageError` events and no worker console error).
